text:
maria: ran an nsys capture of the dedicated inference node during a 512-concurrent request soak. timeline shows large memcpy blocks hugging kernels, and some CPU gaps between batch launches. attaching a quick summary below.
sam: can you paste the nsys command you used? did you collect CUDA API or just kernel traces?
maria: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite --stop-on-exit` then ran the batcher for ~2m. captured api + kernel timelines.
lee: timeline note: I see a long memcpy HtoD on stream 0 ~28ms and then `cudaLaunchKernel` for `attention_kernel_fp16` ~22ms, but they don't overlap in the timeline — memcpy finishes then kernel starts. are we using the default stream anywhere? that would force sync.
maria: exact. top timeline snippet I saw (annotated):
```text
[stream 1] cudaMemcpyAsync HtoD size=4.2MB  duration=28.1ms
[stream 0] cudaLaunchKernel attention_kernel_fp16  duration=22.3ms
```
no overlap, even though memcpy was async.
noah: steps to check: are we accidentally using pageable host memory? cudaMemcpyAsync requires pinned memory to be async. if the batcher allocates std::vector<char> for KV cache copies, it'll fall back to sync memcpy.
sam: also check that the memcpy and kernel are on different non-zero streams. default stream (0) has special semantics and can synchronize with others depending on legacy behavior.
maria: verified: batcher uses arena allocator that uses malloc for KV slices. code path recently changed in the quantized KV cache rewrite — we might have lost cudaMallocHost usage.
lee: that would explain memcpy blocking GPU. Another signal: CPU side shows a 35ms gap between the worker thread issuing the copy and the next batch launch — topo shows worker blocked on `std::mutex` for that time. suspect we do a synchronous fallback path that holds the lock while copying.
maria: copied the perfetto flame: host thread (batcher) has NVTX ranges: `batch_build` -> `kv_copy` -> `enqueue` and during `kv_copy` we call `memcpy` into device buffer. stack traces show path: `Arena::alloc()` -> `std::memcpy` -> `cudaMemcpy` (sync path)
noah: quick repro suggestion: run small reproducer with `cudaMallocHost` pinned buff and cudaMemcpyAsync + cudaStreamSynchronize at end; and compare with pageable memcpy. nvprof/nsys will show overlap difference.
sam: also check kernel selection: I noticed `gpt_fwd_kernel_q4` runtime increased from 7ms to ~11ms after the quantization PR. If memcpy blocks, effective GPU occupancy changes and kernels can take longer due to different SM scheduling. but kernel codepath itself might be different: was a new register tiling applied?
maria: PR #6424 changed the kernel tiling heuristic for q4 models. metrics show launches on stream 2 vs stream 1 previously. I wonder if that plus changed memory path interacts.
lee: two-pronged: 1) fix host -> device copy to use pinned `cudaMallocHost` and ensure `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., streamX)` where streamX != 0. 2) ensure batcher doesn't hold locks during the copy (move copy outside critical section). that'll remove the CPU scheduling gap.
noah: one more gotcha: if you use the CUDA default stream implicitly (kernel launch without stream param or `cudaStreamDefault`), it may synchronize with the legacy per-thread default stream. prefer explicit streams created once per worker and reuse.
maria: did a follow-up nsys after switching to `cudaMallocHost` and moving the copy out of the mutex. new timeline shows memcpy HtoD (~6ms) on stream 3 overlapping with `attention_kernel_fp16` on stream 3 and stream 4 launches. overlap ~80% now. batcher host thread gap reduced to ~4ms.
perf-bot: automated summary: memcpy HtoD reduced from 28.1ms -> 6.2ms after pinned memory, kernel overlap increased, tail latency P99 improved 18%.
sam: awesome. for permanence, add unit test / CI perf job that runs nsys capture baseline on a small fixture and checks for memcpy>kernel blocking on production-like alloc path.
maria: agreed. I'll open a PR to reintroduce `PinnedBuffer` in the arena with a flag controlled by an env var and add an integration test that verifies overlap via a lightweight nsys parsing script.
lee: also warn about `cudaDeviceSynchronize` sprinkled in the model init paths — that can hide perf issues during warmup but kills steady-state overlap. grep for `DeviceSynchronize` in the runtime.
sam: final note: kernel selection regression — let's add microbenchmarks for the tiled attention variants with representative seq-len and KV sizes; make the kernel choice runtime-driven with runtime perf table rather than static heuristic.
maria: thanks all — filing follow-up items: PR for pinned arena + move copy out of lock, CI nsys overlap test, microbench for kernel heuristics. will paste PR links once ready. :thumbsup
